questions: Did the 200-unit field trial include units running in the coldest conditions and at the heaviest heating load, where the changed compressor control logic is under the most stress, or were the trial units mostly in mild conditions?

If a unit misbehaves after the update, can you roll it back remotely and quickly, or could a unit that loses heating stay down until a technician visits? How many technician visits could you actually staff in one week?
What exactly did the last six updates change? If none of them touched compressor control, how much does their clean record tell you about this one?

Has the compressor supplier independently validated the new control logic across the full range of operating conditions and hardware revisions in the installed base, and have they put that sign-off in writing?

How closely does the 200-unit trial group match the 40,000 installed units in hardware revision, age, installer, refrigerant charge, and local climate? Which sub-populations are not represented at all?
Can the energy-saving mode be shipped switched off, or enabled by remote flag, so the firmware reaches everyone Monday while the compressor behaviour change reaches only a small group at first?

What does a staged rollout actually cost you: how many days of delay, and does the campaign have to start with the feature available everywhere, or can it launch with 'rolling out over the next weeks'?

What telemetry will tell you within hours that heating is failing, such as compressor short-cycling, lockouts, or failed defrost cycles, and who is watching it, with what threshold for pausing the rollout, over the weekend and during the first week?
How many customers would lose heating in a plausible failure at this scale, how many of them are vulnerable households, and what is the weather forecast for the regions in the first wave?
What would have to be true for you to prefer the staged option? Is the Monday date fixed by something other than the campaign, or is it a default nobody has questioned?
